01
Classification opening

Four departments say asset. They do not mean the same boundary.

Operations calls a telemetry point an asset. Finance means a capitalized item. Maintenance means equipment that can receive work. Geographic Information System staff include mains, valves, facilities, and sometimes service locations. None of those teams is necessarily careless. They are working inside different scopes.

Start by recording each term, definition, owner, scope, and example. Do not force one word into one universal meaning before you understand the work it performs.

Four teams use asset differently. What is the strongest first move?

Decision check

Choose the strongest answer, then check it. The feedback explains the boundary.

02
Specimen cabinet

A class is a category. An instance is one thing in it.

Pump is a class. Pump P-104 is an instance of that class. Vertical Turbine Pump can be a more specific class beneath Pump. The physical P-104 does not become a subclass merely because it sits below Pump on a slide.

A property expresses a relationship or characteristic. serves can connect Pump P-104 to Pressure Zone 3. preferredLabel can attach readable text. Keep categories, individual things, and relationships visibly different.

Say the definition before turning each card.

Flip-card retrieval

Say the answer before selecting each card. Select all four cards to complete this retrieval check.

03
Classification tree

A taxonomy arranges useful classifications

A taxonomy answers where a term belongs in a hierarchy. Pump can contain Rotodynamic Pump, which can contain Centrifugal Pump. One thing may belong to more than one class when the meanings are compatible and governed.

The hierarchy should serve a question. If maintenance needs equipment type while emergency planning needs criticality class, two coordinated classification dimensions may be clearer than one forced tree.

Match each item to its correct role.

Relationship matching

Match each ordinary-language question to the job that answers it. Check all rows together, then revise any row that needs another look.

04
Hierarchy Consequence Laboratory

RDF Schema declarations have semantic consequences

RDF Schema, usually shortened to RDFS, can say one class is a subclass of another, one property is a subproperty of another, and a property's subjects or objects belong to declared classes. Those statements let software derive additional class membership.

That is why a careless domain declaration can surprise you. If concerns has domain WorkOrder, then anything used as the subject of concerns is inferred to be a WorkOrder. RDFS did not run a form check. It applied the declared meaning.

Hierarchy Consequence Laboratory

Hierarchy consequence laboratory

For each statement, choose Accept, Repair, or Reject. Use the explanation to inspect what RDFS would imply.

VerticalTurbinePump subClassOf Pump

P-104 typed as VerticalTurbinePump is also a Pump.

Pump_P104 subClassOf Pump

One physical pump is incorrectly modeled as a class.

concerns domain WorkOrder

Every subject using concerns is inferred to be a WorkOrder.

locatedAt range Pump

Every object of locatedAt is inferred to be a Pump.

criticalAsset subPropertyOf hasClassification

Every criticalAsset relationship is also a classification relationship.

Review every classification statement.
05
Leader and practitioner view

Definitions need owners, examples, and releases

A definition becomes operational only when people can find its owner, scope, examples, exclusions, effective version, and change route. Publish the vocabulary like a maintained product, not a workshop souvenir.

Keep validation separate. RDFS can describe and imply meaning. Module 10 will use SHACL to check declared structural expectations. A valid shape result still will not prove that a real pump is located where the record says it is.

A property range says Location. What does RDFS do?

Decision check

Choose the strongest answer, then check it. The feedback explains the boundary.

Leader view

Ask who may approve a definition change

06
Professional application

Release a vocabulary another team can use and challenge

Choose one utility term with competing meanings. Record its preferred definition, narrower classes, examples, exclusions, and properties. Name the owner and release state.

Add one semantic consequence and one validation boundary. That final distinction prevents future teams from treating an inference declaration as a data-quality check.

Questions people actually ask

Can one thing belong to several classes?

Yes. Pump P-104 may be a Vertical Turbine Pump and a Critical Asset when both classifications are defined and supported.

Who owns a definition?

Name an accountable domain owner and a review group. Ownership should follow the operational meaning and its consequences.

Does RDFS validate data?

No. RDFS describes semantic relationships and supports inference. SHACL is designed for declared graph validation.

Is every list a taxonomy?

No. A controlled list becomes a taxonomy when governed broader and narrower relationships organize its terms.

What is the danger of a broad domain declaration?

Every subject using that property may be inferred to belong to the domain class

Evidence boundary

Riverbend examples are instructional. W3C RDF Schema defines the vocabulary and semantic conditions taught here. It does not decide utility ownership, terminology policy, or real-world truth.

Module Glossary

controlled vocabulary

An approved set of terms with governed meanings.

taxonomy

A governed broader and narrower classification arrangement.

class

A category of resources.

instance

One resource that belongs to a class.

property

A named relationship or characteristic.

subclass

A class whose members are also members of a broader class.

domain

A class inferred for subjects using a property.

range

A class inferred for objects used with a property.

RDF Schema

The RDF vocabulary for describing classes properties and semantic relationships.
